Add a soft shadow, not a hard one. Shadow strength 40–60 with an offset of 20–30 px gives a natural "floating card" look. Crank it only when the background is very bright.

Choose a frame that matches the context. A browser frame tells people it is a web app and lets you show the domain in the address bar. The Mac or Windows window reads as a desktop app. The phone bezel is for mobile screenshots, ideally with the 9:16 or 4:5 ratio. "None" with 12–16 px corners is the cleanest option for documentation and blog posts.

Give it room to breathe. Padding is the single biggest upgrade. 48–96 px of space around the shot lets the shadow and background do their job; for social posts where the image is shown small, go lower (24–40 px) so the UI stays legible.

Indie makers and startups use it for launch tweets, changelog posts and the "What's new" section of a landing page. Designers wrap UI explorations in a frame before posting to Dribbble or sharing with a client. Technical writers and support teams add padding and a subtle border so screenshots in docs do not bleed into the page background. Marketers batch-style a whole feature set with one preset so every image in a campaign looks consistent.

Pick a contrasting background. A light UI looks sharpest on a dark or saturated gradient (Midnight, Sunset, Ocean); a dark UI pops on Peach, Mono or a pale mesh. The gradient should not fight with your brand colors, so when in doubt use the custom pickers and sample your logo color for one of the two stops.

Screenshot Studio is a static page. When you drop an image it is decoded into memory, drawn onto a canvas together with the background, shadow and frame, and encoded back to PNG or JPG by your browser. There is no upload endpoint and no server-side rendering, so confidential dashboards, unreleased features and customer data never leave your computer. Your style settings are saved in localStorage so the tool opens exactly how you left it.

Screenshot Studio may display advertisements served by Google AdSense to keep the tool free. Google and its partners may use cookies (including the DoubleClick cookie) to serve ads based on your prior visits to this and other websites. You can opt out of personalized advertising at Google Ads Settings or via aboutads.info. Visitors in the EEA and UK will be asked for consent where required.

Screenshot Studio renders mockups entirely inside your web browser using the HTML5 Canvas API. When you drop, pick or paste an image it is decoded into your browser's memory, composed with the background, frame and caption on a canvas, and encoded back to PNG or JPG on your device. No image, filename or pixel data is ever transmitted to our servers or to any third party. There is no upload endpoint. Closing or reloading the page clears the images from memory.
